title: House of Ascania
capsule: The House of Ascania (Askanier) was a German dynastic house originating in the Harz region whose most consequential member, Albert the Bear, established the Margraviate of Brandenburg in formerly Slavic territory around 1157 and became its first margrave. At its height the dynasty simultaneously controlled the Duchy of Saxony, the Duchy of Saxony-Lauenburg, the Principality of Lüneburg, and multiple Anhalt subdivisions — making it one of the most powerful dynasties in the Holy Roman Empire. The main Brandenburg line died out with Waldemar in 1319; Saxony-Wittenberg passed to the Wettins in 1422; the Anhalt cadet branches persisted until the last Ascanian duke abdicated in November 1918 during the German Revolution.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. As a dynastic entity rather than a single polity, the mapped territory depends on which Ascanian branch and date is shown; the multiple non-contiguous Ascanian territories have broadly known but fluctuating boundaries documented through imperial charters.
